I migrated `src/module.ts` to es-toolkit and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks under `--strict`. I did not run any comparison against the original, so equal results on the input range are reasoned, not tested.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `keyBy(rows, fn)` | `keyBy` | Same behaviour. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `sumBy(rows, (row) => row.age)` | The strict `sumBy` takes a function instead of a property name. An empty array returns 0 in both. |
| `sortedUniq` | `uniq` | es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. On ascending input, `uniq` gives the same result. |

There is no lodash import left, no hand-written replacement and no adapter. The exported signatures are unchanged, and I installed nothing.

- **Bundle size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 206 bytes (min+gzip), of which 95 bytes are my own code. I couldn't get a figure for the original: `npm run size -- src/module.ts` crashed, because lodash isn't installed in `node_modules`. So I haven't checked the 95 bytes against the allowance over the original.
- **Type check:** `npx tsc -p .` reports errors only for `src/module.ts`, because lodash and its types are missing. I ran the `out/module.ts` check separately with `npx tsc --noEmit --strict --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler --skipLibCheck out/module.ts`, which passed.
